title: Unconditional Unclonable Encryption
abstract: We give an unconditional construction of information-theoretically secure one-time private-key unclonable encryption scheme for one-bit messages, with efficient encryption and decryption and exponentially small unclonable-indistinguishability advantage.
summary: This paper presents an unconditional construction for a one-time private-key unclonable encryption scheme for single bits. The authors rigorously prove its security by bounding the adversary's advantage using advanced techniques involving operator norms and spectral analysis within quantum information theory. It advances the field by providing tight, information-theoretic security guarantees for this cryptographic primitive.
main_problem: The core problem is constructing an unconditionally secure, information-theoretically secure one-time private-key unclonable encryption (UE) scheme for single-bit messages.
main_result: The authors provide a construction achieving an advantage bound of $	ext{Pr}[	ext{Win}] \le 1/2 + 2^{-(n+1)/2}$, demonstrating the security of the proposed quantum encryption protocol.
method: The proof involves advanced techniques from quantum information theory, utilizing Choi–Jamiołkowski representations and bounding operator norms ($\lVert G_+ Vert_\infty$) derived from analyzing the winning probability in an unclonable indistinguishability game.
model_or_system: The model is a quantum cryptographic scheme operating on one-bit messages using $n$-qubit ciphertexts and classical keys. Security relies fundamentally on the no-cloning principle applied to quantum states.
key_observables: The success probability of an adversary ($	ext{Pr}[	ext{Win}]$) in the unclonable indistinguishability experiment, and related operator norms like $\lVert E_{BC} Vert_\infty$.
important_parameters: The key length $n$ (determining the security parameter), and derived bounds such as $\gamma = d/L$.
main_assumptions: The proof relies on spectral decomposition, bounding quadratic forms using filter operators ($F$), and assuming specific algebraic properties of Pauli operators acting on tensor product Hilbert spaces.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the scheme, formulating the security game in terms of operator traces (Choi states), deriving bounds on correlation operators using lemmas (like Lemma 3.3), and finally applying spectral analysis with filter operators to achieve the tight final bound.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, information-theoretic security proof for a quantum primitive (UE) that is highly relevant to quantum communication protocols, building upon foundational concepts in quantum cryptography.
